instructions: Scrub the squash, halve it and scoop out the seeds. Cut it into 1 inch chunks and leave the skin on. Peel the carrots and potato and cut them into 1 inch chunks too.
Dice the onion and slice the garlic. Chop 2 tbsp of parsley.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and the salt and cook for 4 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the squash, carrots, potato and broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until a knife slides through the squash with no resistance.

Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the cream and blend with an immersion blender, or in batches in a blender, until completely smooth. Fill a blender no more than halfway with hot soup and hold the lid down with a towel.
If it's too thick, stir in a splash of hot water. Add the pepper, then taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve hot with the parsley on top. The soup keeps for 4 days in an airtight container in the fridge, or up to 3 months in the freezer. Reheat it in a pot over low heat, stirring, until steaming.
method_notes: Cuisine Culinaire (the lead) cooks pumpkin, carrots, potato, onion and garlic in water with a stock cube, blends it, and adds cream and parsley to finish. Cooking-EZ's potimarron velouté thickens a plain pumpkin soup with cornflour and cream and says to leave the skin on; this version skips the cornflour and uses vegetable broth in place of water and a stock cube. The lead has only 2 ratings and the best-rated version (Cooking-EZ, 3.9 from 71) is under the 4.0 line, so this is a fallback lead. Kabocha stands in for pumpkin or potimarron.
